stem: A 60-year-old man with long-standing type 2 diabetes has burning pain in both feet that is worse at night and has not eased with ibuprofen. He has reduced pinprick sensation in a stocking distribution. He has an enlarged prostate and already has trouble starting urination.
oneliner: 60M + diabetes + burning foot pain at night + stocking sensory loss + no relief with NSAID + enlarged prostate with hesitancy → which drug?
ask: Which drug is the best next step?

whyNot.A: Already **failed an NSAID**; it does not treat **nerve pain**
whyNot.C: Treats neuropathic pain, but its **antimuscarinic** action can cause **urinary retention** in a man who already has **prostatic hesitancy**
whyNot.D: An opioid is **not first line** for neuropathic pain; first-line drugs are tried first
whyNot.E: Treats **inflammation**, not nerve pain, and would worsen **glucose control** in a diabetic

why: This is **painful diabetic neuropathy**. First-line options are **SNRIs such as duloxetine, gabapentinoids or TCAs**. With **prostatic enlargement**, amitriptyline's **antimuscarinic action** risks **urinary retention**, so duloxetine is the better choice.

drug.name: Duloxetine
drug.how: Inhibits reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine, enhancing descending pain inhibition
drug.use: Diabetic neuropathy, fibromyalgia, depression, generalized anxiety disorder
drug.watch: Nausea, sexual dysfunction, raised blood pressure, serotonin syndrome, hepatotoxicity (avoid in liver disease)

idea.rule: Neuropathic pain responds to SNRIs, TCAs and gabapentinoids, not NSAIDs.
also: Gabapentin and pregabalin are also first line
Topical capsaicin or lidocaine for local neuropathic pain
